script: He bought his own freedom, then secretly freed sixteen more, one at a time, for decades. Frank McWorter was enslaved in Kentucky, but his owner allowed him to run a saltpeter business on the side. He saved every coin from that business in total secret, hiding the true size of his savings from everyone around him. In 1817, he finally had enough to buy his own freedom, and did not stop there. He kept working, kept saving, and one by one bought freedom for his wife, his children, and his grandchildren. He founded his own town in Illinois, and quietly used its land sales to fund even more purchases of freedom. By the time he died, he had personally purchased sixteen family members out of slavery. He bought his own freedom, then spent the rest of his life buying everyone else's.
